full_name: Camiral Golf & Wellness, Stadium Course (formerly PGA Catalunya Resort)

summary.text: The Stadium Course at Camiral Golf & Wellness, formerly PGA Catalunya, is a par 72 championship course designed by Angel Gallardo and Neil Coles and built by the European Tour to rival TPC Sawgrass.

setting.text: The course is laid out in a large pine forest on undulating, at times hilly, ground.
Top100golfcourses describes fir trees, lush vegetation, scrub and purple heather framing each hole, with large lakes that in places form semi-island greens.
It nestles in the Girona mountains just outside the town of Caldes de Malavella.
Every hole can be played from five different tees.
Where2golf says every hole is defended by bunkering and large, fast, undulating greens, and five greens have water close to them.
The 13th is a par four that, where2golf says, offers a panorama of the distant Montseny mountain range.
The club describes mountains and forests as a constant distraction, with trees, bunkers and water hazards waiting to damage a card.

history.text: The course opened in 1999, originally under the name the Green course, when the resort was called PGA Catalunya.
It was the result of more than a decade of European Tour planning, aimed at building its own Players Championship-style course to rival the PGA Tour's TPC Sawgrass.
Within months of opening it hosted the 1999 Gene Sarazen World Open, and then the Spanish Open in 2000.
The Spanish Open returned in 2009, won by Thomas Levet, and in 2014, when Miguel Angel Jimenez won a three-man play-off to become the oldest winner in European Tour history.
The Stadium also hosted the DP World Tour's Catalunya Championship in 2022, according to the club.
The European Tour's Qualifying School Final Stage has been co-hosted at the resort on seven occasions since 2008.
In November 2014 the resort became a candidate venue for Spain's bid for the 2022 Ryder Cup, which Rome won.
In December 2022 the resort rebranded from PGA Catalunya to Camiral Golf & Wellness.
The Stadium Course had a EUR 1 million sustainability-focused upgrade in 2021.
Hole 10 was re-routed in February 2021 into a right-to-left dogleg.
The Ryder Cup was awarded to the Stadium Course for 2031, the 48th edition and Spain's second after Valderrama in 1997.
The resort has been owned by Irish businessman Denis O'Brien since 2008, according to Today's Golfer.

trivia.text: Top100golfcourses says the course has been in its Europe Top 100 since it opened.
In top100golfcourses' 2026 ranking of Spain's courses the Stadium is fourth.
The club says top100golfcourses.com ranked it Spain's number one course from 2012 to 2019.
The club says its 13th hole has been named one of Europe's Top 100 holes.
The Stadium measures 6,684 metres from the back tees at par 72, according to where2golf.
Spain's 1997 Ryder Cup at Valderrama was won by Europe under Seve Ballesteros; the 2031 match will make Spain the first continental European country to host it twice.

1.text: A par four listed at 398 metres. The club advises favouring the right half of the fairway, with water down the left.

2.text: A par four listed at 350 metres where the fairway narrows the further you drive. A severe slope pulls short approaches back into a dell.

3.text: A par five listed at 512 metres, reachable in two by the longest hitters, but the green is set hard against a lake.

5.text: A par three listed at 190 metres with no real safe place to miss the green.

7.text: A par five listed at 535 metres where two big hits might reach the green, with traps close to it.

9.text: The club calls it tough and uncompromising, the longest par four on the course at 437 metres, with a severely sloping green.

10.text: The club says the hole was re-routed in February 2021 into a right-to-left dogleg.

11.text: A par three listed at 172 metres that falls 13 metres from tee to green, so it plays at least a club shorter, with water behind the green.

13.text: The club's signature hole, a par four it says has been named one of Europe's Top 100 holes.
Where2golf says the par-four 13th presents a panorama of the distant Montseny mountain range.

16.text: A par three listed at 183 metres. The green tilts sharply back to front, so the club advises staying below the hole.

17.text: A par four listed at 444 metres, the club advises landing the drive short and right of the fairway bunkers.

18.text: A par four listed at 419 metres, the finishing hole, where the club says there is more room right than left.

local.text: The resort is outside Caldes de Malavella, about 45 minutes north of Barcelona and a few kilometres from Girona airport.
Where2golf places it about 15 km south of Girona.
The resort is in the Costa Brava area of Catalonia, in the foothills of the Pyrenees according to top100golfcourses.
